headline: Bulls gear sells in cold snaps and gift weeks, and a 10.25% tax breeds deal hunters.
summary: The 1990s Bulls and Michael Jordan keep apparel selling through losing seasons, and the 2026-27 rebuild won't change that. Spending peaks in the November-December cold snap, with a second pulse at opening week and a quiet summer. Shoppers split three ways: downtown tourists, neighborhood and mall buyers, and a strong resale layer on the South and West Sides. Tier prices sharply.

insights.title: Heritage outsells the roster
insights.detail: The 1990s Bulls, the Jordan name and the red-and-black Icon look sell whatever the standings say. A 31-51 team with a rebuilding roster gives fans little reason to buy a current-player jersey early.
insights.implication: Lead with Jordan-era graphics, throwback silhouettes and wordmark pieces. Treat Giddey, Buzelis and Wilson jerseys as a smaller, fan-driven layer. Hold rookie product until Wilson proves himself.

insights.title: Winter is the peak, and it's functional
insights.detail: The long, windy cold season (roughly November to March) makes hoodies, heavyweight fleece, puffers, beanies and knit scarves the core volume. Shorts and tees are a compressed June-to-August business.
insights.implication: Weight the Q4 drop toward outerwear, quarter-zips, sherpa and insulated warm-ups in Bulls red and black. Use short-sleeve shooting shirts and tees for summer, the Chicago Marathon and Bears season.

insights.title: Tax and the outlet loop drive deal-hunting
insights.detail: Chicago's combined sales tax is about 10.25%, and clothing is taxed at the general rate. Many suburban and South Side shoppers drive to Chicago Premium Outlets in Aurora, Woodfield in Schaumburg or Oakbrook Center, or buy online.
insights.implication: Plan outlet and promotional tiers on purpose. Use free-shipping thresholds online to offset tax sensitivity at entry price points.

insights.title: Sneaker and resale culture is a parallel economy
insights.detail: Chicago's Jordan lineage feeds a deep sneaker scene: independent boutiques, Sunday swap-meet traders on Maxwell Street and a heavy resale layer. Raffles and in-store lines matter for retro and limited pairs.
insights.implication: Sell Jordan and Bulls-linked product through local shops, in a Chicago-specific drop. For the hype tier, scarcity and a clean raffle beat blanket availability.

insights.title: Gifting bunches up in a few moments
insights.detail: Black Friday through Christmas, Valentine's Day and Father's Day carry the gift buying of jerseys and hoodies. This year the Bulls have no opening-night or Christmas Day game, which removes two national showcases.
insights.implication: Build gift bundles for kids, youth and adults. Push them through the Cup Nights, the home openers and the Bulls-Hawks-Celtics games, not national TV spotlights.

insights.title: A wide income spread and a tourist layer
insights.detail: Spending power runs from affluent North Shore and Gold Coast households to price-sensitive South and West Side neighborhoods. The Magnificent Mile and State Street draw Midwest and international visitors who buy Bulls product as a Chicago souvenir.
insights.implication: Tier it: entry tees and kids at accessible prices, mid-price Swingman and hoodies, premium authentic and collab pieces. Give downtown tourists their own Chicago-skyline and Jordan-heritage graphics.

places.name: United Center
places.why: The Jordan statue outside and the concourse team stores make game days the highest-intent buying moments.

places.name: Magnificent Mile and State Street
places.why: The main tourist and holiday-shopping corridors, packed with Christmas crowds in November and December.

places.name: Chicago Premium Outlets
places.why: The suburban deal-hunting stop for families trading down from downtown prices.

places.name: Woodfield Mall
places.why: One of the region's largest malls and a core suburban stop for the holidays and back-to-school.

places.name: Oakbrook Center
places.why: An affluent western-suburb hub for premium and gift purchases.

places.name: Maxwell Street Market
places.why: A Sunday market with a long tradition of informal sneaker and apparel trading.

places.name: Michael Jordan statue at the United Center
places.why: The most photographed Bulls spot and a natural anchor for pop-ups and photo moments.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.why: The root of Chicago's apparel demand. His name and likeness are licensed, so go through Jordan Brand.

people.name: Josh Giddey
people.why: A lead face of the rebuild and a likely first current-player jersey buy.

people.name: Matas Buzelis
people.why: A homegrown-feeling young star with a strong youth and Lithuanian-diaspora following.

people.name: Caleb Wilson
people.why: The rookie centerpiece. His early play will set the pace for new jersey demand.

people.name: Tiago Splitter
people.why: The new coach, driving the size-and-length identity fans will be watching.

moments.name: Bulls home opener and Cup Nights
moments.why: The season's first buying spike. The Emirates NBA Cup East Group C games against Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte and Washington start Oct 30.

moments.name: Black Friday and holiday gifting
moments.why: The year's biggest sales window, with cold weather pushing outerwear and fleece.

moments.name: Bulls at the Christmas season
moments.why: There's no Christmas Day game this year, so gifting and local pop-ups carry the moment.

moments.name: Valentine's Day and All-Star Weekend
moments.why: Gifting dips and recovers, and All-Star Weekend in Phoenix on Feb 19-21 turns attention to hoops in general.

moments.name: Chicago Marathon
moments.why: A big visitor weekend that lifts downtown retail and running-adjacent apparel.

moments.name: Back-to-school
moments.why: CPS and suburban districts return in mid to late August, which drives kids' and youth sneakers and tees.

designCues.source: Bulls Icon red, the core of the 1990s identity
designCues.use: Lead color on outerwear and tees. Pair with black for the heritage look.

designCues.source: The Bulls Icon and Statement black
designCues.use: Base for hoodies and puffers, so red graphics read in winter light.

designCues.source: The two light-blue stripes of the Chicago municipal flag
designCues.use: Accent stripe or lining on Chicago-specific pieces. The flag's red six-point stars link back to the Bulls palette.

designCues.source: The star motif from the Chicago flag
designCues.use: Embroider or print it sparingly on sleeves, caps and warm-ups. The flag is municipal, so check usage terms.
Premium cold-weather fabrics and insulated shells that feel built for the city.
Use it for heritage graphics on tees and hoodies. Bulls marks need NBA licensing, and Jordan imagery needs Jordan Brand approval.

productHooks: A Q4 cold-weather push of existing heavyweight Bulls hoodies, quarter-zips and insulated warm-ups in red and black this winter. Follow with a new capsule for 2027-28, with flag-blue lining details.
A Jordan-era heritage graphic tee and hoodie line, tiered from entry-price tees to a mid-price premium fleece.
A gift bundle of adult, youth and kids Swingman jerseys, timed to Black Friday and the Cup Nights.
A limited Chicago-only sneaker or apparel drop with local shop partners and a raffle, aimed at the resale-aware buyer.
A rookie capsule for Caleb Wilson and Dailyn Swain, staged after the first month of the season.
watchouts: Jordan imagery, numbers and likeness are controlled through Jordan Brand. Get clearance and don't freelance Jordan graphics.
The Chicago flag is a municipal design. Check the usage rules before putting it on product.
Don't overbuy current-player inventory for a rebuilding team. Heritage sells more reliably than rookie jerseys.
Don't stereotype South and West Side neighborhoods. For any community-linked product, partner with local creators and shops and credit them.

extra.priceProfile: Income runs from very high on the North Side and North Shore to price-sensitive on much of the South and West Sides. A combined city tax of about 10.25% sharpens the deal-hunting. Tier with accessible tees and kids pieces, mid-price hoodies and Swingman, and a small premium authentic and collab layer.
extra.jerseyBehavior: Fans lean toward Swingman and throwback styles for gifts and everyday wear. Collectors buy authentic. Jordan-era numbers and names stay evergreen, while current-player jerseys follow performance. Knockoffs and street resale are common at the low end. Kids and youth are important gifting categories.
